title: Rebuild Lead and Revised Ship Date for a Customer Specification Remake — Plant Scheduling Rule for Factory Production Orders
content:
For Factory Production Orders, the revised ship date of a remake recorded with cause customer specification error is fixed as follows.

**Rebuild start.** The rebuild of a customer specification remake starts on the date of the most recent remake on the order recorded with cause customer specification error.

**Revised ship date.** The remake revised ship date is the rebuild start date plus the class remake lead time in business days, counted starting the day after the rebuild start date, Monday through Friday excluding U.S. federal holidays.

**Figure recorded.** The figure recorded with the remake notice is the remake revised ship date written as the number of calendar days from the date the notice is recorded to that date, negative when that date has already passed.

## Inputs

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| remake date | the most recent remake record on the order with cause customer specification error |
| class remake lead time | the order's build class (business days) |
| notice date | the day the notice is recorded |

## Worked examples (hypothetical, no federal holiday in the period)

- A Custom Size Build order (remake lead time 10 business days) has a customer specification remake recorded on a Wednesday. Counting from the Thursday, the 10th business day is the Wednesday two weeks later. A notice recorded on the Monday five calendar days after the remake records a figure of 9.
- The same remake, with its notice recorded on the Tuesday twenty calendar days after the remake, records a figure of minus 6: the revised ship date passed six calendar days before the notice.
- An order with two customer specification remakes, recorded on different dates, starts the rebuild on the later of the two dates.
